question: Can post-12DK bibliographic/version scholarship materially narrow a lawful reproduction request for NLC call 14202, and do newly surfaced later compilations provide an independent exact-fingerprint witness?
answer: YES TO REPRODUCTION TARGET NARROWING; NO TO A NEW INDEPENDENT FINGERPRINT WITNESS. The official Library Journal landing page identifies Shen Kaiwen's 2025 peer-reviewed bibliographic study. A search-indexed excerpt from the publisher-hosted PDF states that the 1551 Tongshu Leiju bears Yao Kui compilation / Wang Yining collation attribution, and its footnote locates the Jiajing-30 Zhicheng movable-type imprint statement specifically at the end of juan 16, citing Zhang Xiumin (2006:569). Because the NLC copy already survives juan 16-19, this creates a lawful high-value first-pass reproduction target at the end of juan 16. The PDF itself could not be opened through the current web reader because the publisher serves it as application/octet-stream, so this batch treats those interior-page details strictly as secondary scholarly/search-indexed locator evidence, not direct physical-page collation. Separately, a newly surfaced Gujin Tushu Jicheng volume reproduces the same high-information Dahan/Yushui fingerprint, but the volume explicitly labels the section Sanming Tonghui 5; therefore it is downstream reuse of Sanming material, not an independent pre-1578 carrier or second numeric vote.
